coverage.note: Performance: 200 ms over a 10,000-row store on both endpoints; statement count independent of the resolved range's day count; series work range-bounded. The fixture's date span is pinned to 365 distinct UTC days so the measured in-process work is a fixed quantity. Instrument: the FR8.9 fixture and sqlite3 trace hook. NOTE: the concurrency posture is NOT an NFR1.y target — it has no inception NFR parent and is carried separately as a functionally-sourced constraint (FR1.6, BR6.3, FR8.4); see the reverse entry 'Concurrency constraint'.

coverage.target: NFR2.1, NFR2.2, NFR2.3, NFR2.4, NFR2.5, NFR2.6
coverage.note: Security: unchanged loopback/unauthenticated posture; no new egress; parameter-bound statements; enforced loopback bind; no credential anywhere; privacy/compliance within C-9/C-10/C-11. Instruments that exist now: import/static inspection, the armed offline guard (FR8.5), the startup-enforcement test, the existing redaction assertions and the dependency-cap assertion. The FR7.3 secret scanner does NOT exist yet and is a u4-platform-packaging obligation — recorded as a cross-unit dependency, not as this unit's instrument.

Read-only guarantee: no write, no schema change, no access bookkeeping; no mutating statement in the read path. Instrument: the before/after store comparison (row count, schema, content hash) and the sqlite3 trace hook.

coverage.target: NFR4.1, NFR4.2, NFR4.3, NFR4.4, NFR4.5, NFR4.6, NFR4.7
coverage.note: Reliability: 422 naming its field; 500 STORAGE_FAILURE distinct from validation; a failure never renders as an empty result; refuse-never-substitute for every null; idempotent additive migration (sourced to FR5.1–FR5.7, not to NFR3/NFR4); per-section graceful degradation; no silent retry. Instruments: the FR8.2 refusal-shape tests, the US8.5.2 500 test, the FR6.7 view tests, the BR5 migration tests and the AC6.5.2 out-of-order test.

Compatibility (/v1 freeze, envelope shape, SentimentClient and config convention unchanged). This is an invariant the change must not break, not a target with a measurable value: there is no threshold to derive an NFR5.y from. Mapped to BR4.7 (the /v1 freeze) and verified by the existing suite staying green; recorded here as N/A rather than OK-with-a-non-id-target, with the substantive mapping in the reverse array.

Maintainability (module conventions, typed, no third-party validator, no junk-drawer). An invariant of the codebase's own conventions rather than a numeric target; there is no value to sub-number. Mapped to BR2.15 and the tech-stack selections, enforced by the pinned ruff rule set; recorded as N/A with the mapping in the reverse array.

Testability (real SQLite and real served markup, never a double of the subject; no browser automation). It constrains how the instruments above are built rather than being a target itself; no NFR7.y value exists. Mapped to BR6.6 and the team testing posture; recorded as N/A with the mapping in the reverse array.

Observability: a failure reaches the application log through the module logger; the envelope code and the log agree; no request parameter interpolated into statement text and no credential in any log record. Instruments that exist now: the failure-logging test, the BR4.6 inspection and the existing redaction assertions. NOTE: the FR7.3 secret scanner is a u4-platform-packaging dependency, not this unit's instrument.

Scalability: series length equals the days in the resolved range; no response grows with the store; the unbounded series is deliberately uncapped; statement count does not grow with the range span. Instruments: the BR3 series-extent tests, the BR2.4/BR2.6 limit tests and the FR8.9 trace hook.

reverse.note: The cross-thread concurrency posture (two overlapping requests raise no cross-thread error; BR6.3 requires the test red if thread affinity is reverted). Recorded across performance-requirements.md § 'Concurrency posture' and reliability-requirements.md § 'Concurrency — a functionally-sourced constraint carried for traceability'.
